title: Patchify and unpatchify
goal:
Section 3.1 reshapes an image $x \in \mathbb{R}^{H \times W \times C}$ into $N = HW/P^2$ flattened patches $x_p \in \mathbb{R}^{N \times (P^2 \cdot C)}$. Write `patchify(img, P)` and its exact inverse `unpatchify(patches, H, W, C, P)`.

Patches come in raster order: left to right along the first patch row, then the next row. Inside a patch, flatten the pixels in `(row, column, channel)` order. Use only `reshape` and `transpose`. Nothing is computed or lost, so `unpatchify(patchify(img, P), ...)` must return the original image exactly.
hints: Split each spatial axis in two first: `img.reshape(H // P, P, W // P, P, C)`. The axes are now (patch row, row in patch, patch column, column in patch, channel).
Move the two patch-grid axes to the front with `transpose(0, 2, 1, 3, 4)`, then reshape to `(N, P * P * C)`.
Without the transpose, `reshape(N, P * P * C)` runs without an error but puts pixels from different patches in one row.

`unpatchify` applies the same steps in reverse order: reshape to `(H // P, W // P, P, P, C)`, transpose with `(0, 2, 1, 3, 4)` again (it swaps axes 1 and 2, so it is its own inverse), and reshape to `(H, W, C)`.
